links.outcome: Concordance with expert-adjudicated final decisions versus tool-free LLMs and neurologists on the same cases
links.effect: StrokeAgent 86% concordance, exceeding tool-free LLMs by 13 points and six neurologists by 17 points; complete-pathway concordance 76%.
links.quote: StrokeAgent achieved 86% concordance with expert-adjudicated final decisions, exceeding the mean performance of three tool-free large language models (LLMs) and six resident and attending neurologists by 13 and 17 percentage points, respectively, under matched information content and timing.

unlisted_practices: Temporal alignment and sequential decision-point updating of AI recommendations across the care pathway
Auditable chains of supporting findings and evidence for each recommendation

screen.reason: Evaluates StrokeAgent, a multimodal agentic decision-support system, compared to clinicians and baseline LLMs on a retrospective cohort of 100 patient cases, assessing concordance, decision time, reasoning quality, and potential harm.
